title: Pre-Market — Thursday, Nov 12, 2026
html:
Nvidia's boardroom drama drags the open, and SPY slips back to its 50% line. Here's what I'm seeing before the bell. One company's leadership crisis is pulling the Nasdaq lower this morning; the rest of the market is barely moving.

The one thing

SPY is at $756.96 pre-market, 21 cents under the 50% line at $757.17. As long as it holds above $751.39, yesterday's bounce is still alive. The $765 call trigger is further away today, not closer.

Nvidia is down 7.8% to $160.26 after reports its board is weighing whether to replace CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia is about 10% of the Nasdaq 100 and about 5% of the S&P 500, so one stock is doing most of the damage. That is a headline about one company, not about the economy, and a board decision could land at any hour, so expect jumpy swings in both directions.

Overnight in plain words

  • US futures: S&P 500 about −0.4%, Nasdaq 100 about −0.8% to −1.0%, the Dow roughly flat. SPY $756.96 (−0.4%), QQQ $685.46 (−0.7%).
  • Asia and Europe: Nikkei −0.7%, Hang Seng −1.2%, Kospi −0.6%. Europe's Stoxx 600 closed at a record yesterday (+0.7%).
  • Oil: WTI about $86.8 and Brent about $93, a small bounce off a two-month low ($91.6 Brent). Iran talks are stuck on the Strait of Hormuz.
  • Rates and fear: the bond market reopens after Veterans Day with the 10-year at 4.99% and the 2-year at 4.77%. Futures price about a 93% chance of a December rate hike. The VIX closed at 17.49 (VIX futures 18.85).
  • The headline: Bernstein (target $200), Evercore ($186) and Oppenheimer downgraded Nvidia this morning; Cantor kept its Buy but cut to $250. Washington is also pushing a fresh crackdown on chips reaching China.

SPY at the open

Pre-market: $756.96

  • Oct 6 record high · target 2: $781.62
  • 78.6% of the drop · target 1: $771.15
  • Ceiling · 61.8% + 50-day · trigger: $763–765
  • 50% of the drop: $757.17
  • 38.2% · keeps the bounce alive: $751.39
  • Old floor · 23.6%: $744–745
  • 200-day + Nov 5 low: $729–733

How I read it: the pre-market price sits right on the 50% line of the Oct 6 → Nov 5 drop. The ceiling is still $763–765 (61.8% line $762.94 + 50-day $764.55). The line that keeps the bounce alive is $751.39.

  • If SPY opens above $757.17 and holds it after the first 30 minutes, the bounce is intact; the ceiling at $763–765 is the next test, and $765 is still the trigger for the $780 call.
  • If it holds between $751.39 and $757.17, it's a chop zone. Nothing triggers. Sit on your hands and let Nvidia's news play out.
  • If it opens below $751.39, yesterday was only a relief bounce. Next floor is the old $744–745 zone; no new calls.

Movers on your list (Watchlist)

  • NVDA $160.26 (−7.8%): Board weighing CEO Huang's future; four analyst cuts. Broke below last night's floor: the 1.618 down-extension $166.29 and the Mar 30 low $163.90. Next on the map: your 0.5 at $155.33, then the 2.0 down-extension $153.61. Only a close counts. Still avoid: earnings Nov 17 sit inside every contract.
  • SMCI $28.90 (−5.0%): Chip give-back. No change; no play.
  • DRAM $43.43 (−3.2%): Memory give-back. No change.
  • MU $786.73 (−3.0%): Gives back part of yesterday's +11.9%. Exactly why we didn't chase it. No change.
  • DELL $363.00 (−2.9%): AI-server give-back. Still above its 200-day ($340.20), so the downside idea stays paused. Under $340 revives it.
  • BE $203.73 (−2.7%): Chip-adjacent give-back. Between your 0.786 ($156.28) and 1.382 ($227.97). No change.
  • SMH $494.78 (−2.4%): Nvidia is its biggest holding. The downside idea watches $427, still 14% away. No change.
  • AMD $566.32 (+2.4%): Money rotating from Nvidia to rivals (Broadcom up too). No contract under $800 ($3,267 for the nearest call). Watch only.
  • ORCL $125.60 (−2.2%): AI-debt worry returns after an 8.8% bounce. The put setup wants a failed rally into the 50-day (~$137); it's moving away from that zone. Earnings Dec 14 sit inside the Dec 18 contracts.

Also: PLTR $170.16 (−1.3%) is under yesterday's low; see the plays below. XOM $167.82 (+0.7%) is above your 2.0 extension at $166.89 pre-market, after four days capped there; it needs a close above it to count (next: the 2.382 at $174.69). NOW $101.00 (−1.7%) leans the way the downside idea wants, with no new trigger. DAL, HLT and the travel names are flat.

Today's calendar (ET)

  • 8:30 AM: Weekly jobless claims (195K expected (prior 189K))
  • 9:00 AM: Fed's Hammack speaks (voter)
  • 10:00 AM: Existing home sales (Oct) · Fed's Barr (voter)
  • 11:15 AM: Fed's Goolsbee speaks
  • 1:00 PM: 30-year Treasury auction (first bond test since the hot CPI)
  • 1:10–1:30 PM: Fed's Daly, then Schmid
  • 6:30 PM: Fed's Williams (voter)
  • After close: Cisco, Applied Materials (AMAT moves SMH and the chip group)

No watchlist name reports tonight, so no IV-crush risk tonight. Ahead: October PPI tomorrow at 8:30 AM; Nvidia reports Tue Nov 17 after the close; DELL Nov 24. Anyone holding NVDA or DELL options through those dates faces IV crush (the option's extra premium draining right after the report). Nvidia's board news could hit at any time today.

Plays check (Options Playbook)

Option quotes below are from yesterday's close (options don't trade before the bell). "IV vs moves" compares the option's implied volatility with the stock's actual moves over the last 60 days.

  • PLTR Dec 18 $180 call (open) — Still valid, under pressure. PLTR is $170.16 pre-market, below yesterday's low $170.80: that's the early warning from last night's plan, not the exit. The exit is a close below $158, 7% away. This is last night's homework question come to life. My take: hold to the plan, because the dip is Nvidia's news rubbing off, not Palantir's. Don't add, and judge it at the close. OI 8,527 · vol 439 · bid/ask $7.35/$7.55 (2.7%) · delta 0.39 · IV 47% vs moves 50% → FAIR (0.93) · no earnings inside
  • DAL Dec 18 $90 call (open) — Still valid. DAL $91.29, flat. Oil is steady near $87, so nothing changed. Target 2 $95.18; stop DAL below $83. The quote is wide, so any sale goes in as a limit near the mid. OI 3,138 · vol 23 · bid/ask $5.00/$5.80 (14.8%, wide) · delta 0.59 · IV 37% vs moves 36% → FAIR (1.02) · no earnings inside
  • HLT Dec 18 $380 call (open) — Still valid. HLT flat at $376.91. Target 1 $385.93 is 2.4% away; exit on a close below $359.41. Thin contract: sell with a limit. OI 282 · vol 6 · bid/ask $9.60/$12.50 (26%, thin) · IV 24% vs moves 23% → FAIR (1.04) · no earnings inside
  • SPY Dec 18 $780 call (watching) — Wait (further from trigger). Trigger is SPY above $765.00, now 1.1% away, versus 0.7% last night. Exit line $751.39. Targets $771.15, $781.62. OI 38,270 · vol 1,987 · bid/ask $5.23/$5.28 (1%) · delta 0.24 · IV 12% vs moves 15% → CHEAP (0.80) · no earnings inside
  • BA Dec 18 $170 put (watching) — Wait. BA $173.58 (−0.6%). Trigger below $165.00 (4.9% away) or a failed rally into $179–181.5 (3.4% above). The $170 put's spread still fails the 10% rule; the backup Dec $165 put passes ($2.77/$3.05, 9.6%, OI 6,161, vol 394, delta −0.29, CHEAP 0.87). OI 4,087 · vol 533 · bid/ask $4.15/$4.80 (14.5%, fails) · delta −0.39 · IV 31% vs moves 36% → CHEAP (0.85) · no earnings inside

No new plays. Nvidia's drop isn't a setup that fits the rules: its report on Nov 17 sits inside every contract, and its options will be pricey after a 7.8% gap. AMD's rotation bounce has no contract under $800.

Alerts for today

  • SPY — price crosses above $765.00 → call trigger for the $780 call
  • SPY — price crosses below $751.39 → the bounce is failing; no new calls
  • PLTR — price crosses below $160.00 → getting close to the $158 exit line (it's a close rule)
  • BA — price crosses below $165.00 → put trigger (check the spread first)
  • DAL — price crosses above $95.18 → target 2, take profit on the $90 call

An alert means look now, not buy now.

Opening rule of the day

Don't trade the headline gap in the first 30 minutes. Today's gap is about one company's boardroom, and a single announcement can flip it in seconds. Let the first 30 minutes settle, then judge SPY against $757.17 and $751.39. Remember the exits in the plan are close rules: a 9:35 AM dip in PLTR is information, not an order. And if you sell DAL or HLT, use a limit order near the mid; those spreads are wide.

Educational only, not personalized investment advice. Claude never places trades.
